learning_objective: 🎯 Understand how to break down long, intimidating texts into smaller, readable sections by giving them informative mini-headings.

key_vocabulary.hindi_meaning: बदलाव (एक विचार से दूसरे में जाना)

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Sub-titling is the practice of adding mini-headings (sub-titles) to different sections of a long article or essay to tell the reader what that specific section is about.
Long walls of text are boring and hard to read. Sub-titles break the text into manageable 'chunks', improving readability and helping the reader scan for information quickly.
A new sub-title is needed whenever the text shifts to a new idea. For example, moving from 'Causes of Pollution' to 'Effects of Pollution' requires a new sub-title.
A good sub-title is short, catchy, and accurately reflects the content of the paragraph below it. It shouldn't be a full sentence.
The main Title is at the top (largest or boldest). Sub-titles are placed throughout the text. This creates a visual hierarchy that guides the reader's eyes.

fun_activity.title: 📰 The Newspaper Editor
fun_activity.instructions: Take a long article from today's newspaper that has no sub-headings. Read it and draw a line wherever the topic slightly changes. Give a 2-3 word sub-title for each section you created!

exam_tips: 📌 When asked to provide sub-titles for a passage, read each paragraph and ask yourself: 'What is the ONE main point of this paragraph?' That answer is your sub-title.
📌 Keep sub-titles uniform. If your first sub-title is a question (e.g., 'What is Stress?'), try to make the others questions too (e.g., 'How to Manage It?').
📌 Sub-titles should be underlined or written in bold to stand out from the main text.
quick_recap: ⭐ Sub-titles act as signposts on a road, telling the reader exactly where the text is taking them.
⭐ They are heavily used in magazines, blogs, and textbooks to make reading less tiring.
⭐ A title covers the WHOLE text; a sub-title covers only a SPECIFIC section.
